note: Planted secrets issues. Match by file + issue; line +-3 counts. Decoys must NOT be reported. All values are labelled fakes; score on where secrets live, not the values.

vulns.title: Production .env with live-style Stripe key committed to the repo
Admin API key hardcoded in source
Same JWT secret in .env, as code fallback, and in the CI workflow (deploy.yml:24): one forgeable-token key across prod, staging and source (cross-file)
Long-lived AWS access key pair hardcoded in workflow env instead of OIDC/secrets
.gitignore does not exclude .env (or key files), which is why .env got committed
App connects to the database as the postgres superuser; no least-privilege scoping
/debug/env endpoint returns the whole process environment, unauthenticated
Admin API key accepted in the query string, lands in logs and history
Deploy token echoed to CI logs (with set -x tracing on)
Stripe key passed as docker build-arg, baked into image layers
Production Stripe key used as the fallback for every environment; no per-env scoped key
Rotation only untracks .env; secrets stay in git history, no purge and no revoke of old keys
New key written to a world-readable /tmp file and printed to stdout
gitleaks hook set to manual stage, so commits are not blocked
Global exclude skips .env and config/, the exact places secrets live
Third-party action pinned to @master receives the deploy token
JWT lifetime of 3650 days: stolen tokens effectively never expire
All request headers, including Authorization, logged

decoys.why: obviously fake test-only values, used only by tests
correct use of secrets.* via env, not echoed or hardcoded
